items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Lenny Niehaus; the interviewer mentions Niehaus as an example of a player Kenton hired, but the interviewee's response focuses entirely on their own experience with Stan Kenton.

ctx.x: “Tampico”. Those were his bread and butter songs.
But he hired a lot of good players and gave a lot of good writers their break like Holman or Lenny Niehaus, or Rugolo, or Graettinger, on and on. Let’s talk about the experience you had.

I had some kids by then so the thought of traveling was not the most tempting thing in one sense and probably tempting in another sense; that I was finally having a steady job with a situation, I didn’t know yet but assumed, was going to have some kind of security in that way that I never had. I was pleased when I heard the band the first time in a theater in Chicago and seeing him [Kenton] do his “Andre Kostelanetz” conducting. It was very moving. Ten brass, wow.
